input.content:
# Blast Radius — Architecture

> Impact-aware PR review powered by Entire Graph.
> Track 02 · Build with Graph Intelligence — Bangalore Tech Week Hackathon.

This document is the map. If you are a fresh agent session reconstructing this
project, read this file top to bottom, then `docs/PLAN.md`, then `src/cli.ts`
and follow the wiring in `src/composition-root.ts`.

---

## 1. What it does (in one paragraph)

When a pull request lands, Blast Radius asks Entire Graph for the real
dependency blast radius of every changed symbol — callers, callees, type
consumers, data flows, co-change files, service boundaries. It cross-checks
that radius against the **stated intent** of the change (the PR description, a
linked issue, or an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer) and flags anything touched
that falls outside the original ask. It then ranks the affected tests by
proximity in the graph and proposes a minimal-but-sufficient test set instead
of "run everything". The reviewer gets one comment: *"This change touches 14
nodes, 3 outside stated intent — here are the 6 tests that actually cover it"*,
every claim linking back to the graph path that justifies it.

It uses the graph as a **real dependency**, not a viewer: `diff`, `impact`,
`neighbors`, and `snapshot` output is consumed, joined, scored, and turned into
a decision. Raw graph output is never shown on its own.

---

## 2. Design principles

| Principle | How it shows up |
| --- | --- |
| **Hexagonal (Ports & Adapters)** | The domain core (`src/domain/`) has zero I/O. It depends only on interfaces declared in `src/ports/`. Every external system — the `entire-graph` binary, GitHub, git, the filesystem — is an adapter behind a port. |
| **Dependency Inversion** | Core defines the interfaces it needs; adapters implement them. Nothing in `domain/` imports from `adapters/`. |
| **Single composition root** | All wiring happens in `src/composition-root.ts`. No `new SomeAdapter()` scattered through the code. Swapping an implementation is a one-line change there. |
| **Pure pipeline stages** | Analysis is a chain of pure functions `Stage<In, Out>` composed in `src/domain/pipeline.ts`. Each stage is unit-tested in isolation with plain objects. |
| **Strategy pattern for judgement calls** | Scope-creep detection is a set of interchangeable `ScopeCreepStrategy` implementations combined by a `CompositeStrategy`. Adding or changing a heuristic never touches the pipeline. |
| **Result types over exceptions** | Adapter calls that can fail (`binary missing`, `git error`, `network`) return `Result<T, BlastRadiusError>`. Exceptions do not cross the port boundary. |
| **Validate at the boundary** | Every blob of external JSON (entire-graph output, GitHub API) is parsed through a `zod` schema the moment it enters. The domain only ever sees validated value objects. |
| **DRY via shared value objects** | `Symbol`, `GraphNode`, `RadiusNode`, `IntentModel`, `Finding`, `TestCandidate` are declared once in `src/domain/model.ts` and reused everywhere. |

---

## 3. Data flow

```
                      ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   git base..head ───▶│  cli.ts  →  composition-root.ts  →  app/review │
                      └───────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                              │  (ports injected)
                    ┌─────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┐
                    ▼                         ▼                          ▼
          GraphProvider port          IntentSource port           ReportSink port
                    │                         │                          │
   ┌────────────────┴───────┐      ┌───────────┴─────────┐     ┌──────────┴──────────┐
   │ EntireGraphCliAdapter  │      │ CompositeIntentSrc  │     │ GitHubCommentSink   │
   │ FixtureGraphAdapter    │      │  ├ PrBody           │     │ StdoutSink          │
   │                        │      │  ├ GitHubIssue      │     │ FileSink            │
   └────────────────────────┘      │  └ CheckpointTrailer│     └─────────────────────┘
                                   └─────────────────────┘

   DOMAIN PIPELINE  (src/domain/pipeline.ts — pure, no I/O)

   ChangeSet ─▶ BlastRadius ─▶ ┌── ScopeCheck ───┐
   (diff)       (impact ×N,    ├── TestSelection ┤─▶ AnalysisReport ─▶ Renderer ─▶ Sink
                 unioned)      └── RadiusSummary ─┘   (Builder)          (port)
```

### Stage contracts

| Stage | Input | Output | Pure? | Port used |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `collectChangeSet` | `{base, head}` | `ChangeSet` (changed symbols + `dependents_count`) | no | `GraphProvider.diff` |
| `computeBlastRadius` | `ChangeSet` | `BlastRadius` (deduped `RadiusNode[]`, bucketed by relation) | no | `GraphProvider.impact` per symbol |
| `resolveIntent` | `PrContext` | `IntentModel` | no | `IntentSource.get` |
| `detectScopeCreep` | `ChangeSet + IntentModel` | `Finding[]` | **yes** | — |
| `selectTests` | `BlastRadius` | `TestPlan` (ranked `TestCandidate[]` + run command + coverage gaps) | **yes** | — |
| `summarizeRadius` | `BlastRadius` | `RadiusSummary` (counts by module / service / relation) | **yes** | — |
| `buildReport` | all of the above | `AnalysisReport` | **yes** | — (Builder) |

The three impure stages are thin: they call a port, validate the response, and
map it to a value object. All judgement lives in the pure stages, which is what
makes the tests fast and the curveball cheap to absorb.

---

## 4. Module layout

```
blast-radius/
├── src/
│   ├── domain/                    pure core — no imports from adapters/ or node built-ins for I/O
│   │   ├── model.ts               value objects + zod schemas (single source of truth)
│   │   ├── errors.ts              BlastRadiusError hierarchy + Result<T,E> helpers
│   │   ├── pipeline.ts            Stage<In,Out>, compose(), run()
│   │   ├── blast-radius.ts        union / dedupe / bucket impact results
│   │   ├── summary.ts             counts by module, service, relation
│   │   ├── test-selection.ts      proximity ranking, minimal-set greedy cover, run-command synthesis
│   │   ├── report.ts             AnalysisReportBuilder
│   │   └── scope-creep/
│   │       ├── strategy.ts        ScopeCreepStrategy interface + CompositeStrategy
│   │       ├── keyword-overlap.ts intent keywords vs changed-symbol name tokens
│   │       └── dependents.ts      wide-reaching-change heuristic
│   ├── ports/                     interfaces only, no logic
│   │   ├── graph-provider.ts
│   │   ├── intent-source.ts
│   │   ├── report-sink.ts
│   │   └── renderer.ts
│   ├── adapters/
│   │   ├── graph/
│   │   │   ├── entire-graph-cli.ts   shells out to the real binary (execa)
│   │   │   └── fixture.ts            reads fixtures/entire-graph/*.json  (dev + tests + offline)
│   │   ├── intent/
│   │   │   ├── pr-body.ts
│   │   │   ├── github-issue.ts       `gh issue view --json`
│   │   │   ├── checkpoint-trailer.ts reads `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer + optional .entire/intent/<id>.json
│   │   │   └── composite.ts          first non-empty wins, records which source answered
│   │   ├── sink/
│   │   │   ├── stdout.ts
│   │   │   ├── github-comment.ts     `gh pr comment --body-file` (upsert: edits its own previous comment)
│   │   │   └── file.ts
│   │   └── render/
│   │       ├── markdown.ts
│   │       ├── json.ts
│   │       └── sarif.ts              findings as SARIF → GitHub code-scanning tab
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── review.ts                the use-case; wires stages into a pipeline and runs it
│   │   └── config.ts               zod config schema, env + flag merge
│   ├── composition-root.ts         Factory: build the adapter set from config
│   └── cli.ts                      commander; parse args → composition root → review()
├── test/
│   ├── domain/                     pure unit tests (majority of the suite)
│   ├── adapters/                   adapter tests against recorded fixtures / fakes
│   └── e2e/                        full pipeline on fixtures/scenarios/*
├── fixtures/
│   ├── entire-graph/               recorded `diff`, `impact`, `neighbors` JSON
│   └── scenarios/                  end-to-end PR scenarios (input + expected report snapshot)
├── action.yml                      composite GitHub Action
├── .github/workflows/
│   ├── ci.yml
│   └── blast-radius.yml            self-dogfood: runs Blast Radius on this repo's own PRs
└── docs/  ARCHITECTURE.md · PLAN.md · DEMO.md
```

**Import rule (enforced by an eslint boundary rule):**
`domain/` → may import `domain/` only.
`ports/` → may import `domain/model` only.

# Blast Radius — Architecture

> Impact-aware PR review powered by Entire Graph.
> Track 02 · Build with Graph Intelligence — Bangalore Tech Week Hackathon.

This document is the map. If you are a fresh agent session reconstructing this
project, read this file top to bottom, then `docs/PLAN.md`, then `src/cli.ts`
and follow the wiring in `src/composition-root.ts`.

---

## 1. What it does (in one paragraph)

When a pull request lands, Blast Radius asks Entire Graph for the real
dependency blast radius of every changed symbol — callers, callees, type
consumers, data flows, co-change files, service boundaries. It cross-checks
that radius against the **stated intent** of the change (the PR description, a
linked issue, or an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer) and flags anything touched
that falls outside the original ask. It then ranks the affected tests by
proximity in the graph and proposes a minimal-but-sufficient test set instead
of "run everything". The reviewer gets one comment: *"This change touches 14
nodes, 3 outside stated intent — here are the 6 tests that actually cover it"*,
every claim linking back to the graph path that justifies it.

It uses the graph as a **real dependency**, not a viewer: `diff`, `impact`,
`neighbors`, and `snapshot` output is consumed, joined, scored, and turned into
a decision. Raw graph output is never shown on its own.

---

## 2. Design principles

| Principle | How it shows up |
| --- | --- |
| **Hexagonal (Ports & Adapters)** | The domain core (`src/domain/`) has zero I/O. It depends only on interfaces declared in `src/ports/`. Every external system — the `entire-graph` binary, GitHub, git, the filesystem — is an adapter behind a port. |
| **Dependency Inversion** | Core defines the interfaces it needs; adapters implement them. Nothing in `domain/` imports from `adapters/`. |
| **Single composition root** | All wiring happens in `src/composition-root.ts`. No `new SomeAdapter()` scattered through the code. Swapping an implementation is a one-line change there. |
| **Pure pipeline stages** | Analysis is a chain of pure functions `Stage<In, Out>` composed in `src/domain/pipeline.ts`. Each stage is unit-tested in isolation with plain objects. |
| **Strategy pattern for judgement calls** | Scope-creep detection is a set of interchangeable `ScopeCreepStrategy` implementations combined by a `CompositeStrategy`. Adding or changing a heuristic never touches the pipeline. |
| **Result types over exceptions** | Adapter calls that can fail (`binary missing`, `git error`, `network`) return `Result<T, BlastRadiusError>`. Exceptions do not cross the port boundary. |
| **Validate at the boundary** | Every blob of external JSON (entire-graph output, GitHub API) is parsed through a `zod` schema the moment it enters. The domain only ever sees validated value objects. |
| **DRY via shared value objects** | `Symbol`, `GraphNode`, `RadiusNode`, `IntentModel`, `Finding`, `TestCandidate` are declared once in `src/domain/model.ts` and reused everywhere. |

---

## 3. Data flow

```
                      ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   git base..head ───▶│  cli.ts  →  composition-root.ts  →  app/review │
                      └───────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                              │  (ports injected)
                    ┌─────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┐
                    ▼                         ▼                          ▼
          GraphProvider port          IntentSource port           ReportSink port
                    │                         │                          │

   │ EntireGraphCliAdapter  │      │ CompositeIntentSrc  │     │ GitHubCommentSink   │
   │ FixtureGraphAdapter    │      │  ├ PrBody           │     │ StdoutSink          │
   │                        │      │  ├ GitHubIssue      │     │ FileSink            │

   (diff)       (impact ×N,    ├── TestSelection ┤─▶ AnalysisReport ─▶ Renderer ─▶ Sink

| `summarizeRadius` | `BlastRadius` | `RadiusSummary` (counts by module / service / relation) | **yes** | — |
| `buildReport` | all of the above | `AnalysisReport` | **yes** | — (Builder) |

# Blast Radius — Build Plan

Track 02 · Build with Graph Intelligence.
Hackathon build day: **Sunday, Sep 6**. Noon Curve Ball at **12:00 IST**.
This plan is written so a fresh agent session can pick it up cold.

---

## 0. Status board

| Phase | State |
| --- | --- |
| P0 Fixtures + scaffold | ☐ |
| P1 Domain model + pipeline harness | ☐ |
| P2 Blast radius stage | ☐ |
| P3 Scope-creep strategies | ☐ |
| P4 Test selection | ☐ |
| P5 Renderers (markdown/json/sarif) | ☐ |
| P6 Adapters (graph cli, intent, sink) | ☐ |
| P7 CLI + composition root | ☐ |
| P8 GitHub Action + demo repo | ☐ |
| P9 Dogfood + snapshot lock | ☐ |
| P10 Pitch deck + recording | ☐ |

Update the boxes as you go. Each phase ends with `npm test` green.

---

## 1. Ground rules

1. **TDD.** Write the failing test first for every `domain/` unit. Red → green → commit.
2. **No `new Adapter()` outside `composition-root.ts`.**
3. **Nothing external is trusted.** Parse every JSON blob through a `zod` schema on entry.
4. **Conventional commits** (`feat:`, `fix:`, `test:`, `docs:`, `chore:`) — tomorrow's
   reconstruction reads these.
5. **Every port ships with a fake.** A port without a test double is not done.
6. Keep the domain free of Node I/O modules. If `domain/` imports `fs` or `child_process`, stop.

---

## 2. Tooling

| Concern | Choice | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Language | TypeScript, ESM, Node ≥ 20 (dev on 24) | one language across CLI + Action |
| Test runner | vitest | TS-native, fast, snapshot support |
| Schema validation | zod | boundary validation + inferred types |
| CLI parsing | commander | standard, minimal |
| Subprocess | execa | safe argv, promises, no shell injection |
| Lint | eslint + `eslint-plugin-boundaries` | enforces the hexagonal import rule |
| Format | prettier | zero-config |
| Build | `tsc` → `dist/`, `bin` → `dist/cli.js` | no bundler to debug |
| GitHub API | `gh` CLI via execa | already on the runner; no Octokit tree |

`package.json` scripts: `build`, `test`, `test:watch`, `lint`, `typecheck`,
`review` (`node dist/cli.js review`).

🧨 Blast Radius

Impact-aware PR review, powered by Entire Graph.
Know what a change really touches, whether it drifted from the ask, and the smallest test set that actually covers it — before you approve.

Bangalore Tech Week Hackathon · Track 02 — Build with Graph Intelligence

--- ## The problem Two things happen on almost every pull request: 1. **The reviewer can't see the blast radius.** A three-line diff to a shared helper can ripple through 20 call sites and three services. The diff doesn't show that. The reviewer approves on vibes. 2. **CI runs everything.** No signal about which tests actually exercise the changed code, so the whole suite runs on every push — slow feedback, wasted minutes, and *still* no confidence the right paths were covered. And a quieter one: **the change quietly grew.** The ticket said "add rate limiting to one endpoint"; the PR also refactored a database signature. Nobody flagged it because nobody cross-checked the diff against the original intent. ## What Blast Radius does On every PR, it runs a pipeline over the Entire Graph: ``` changed symbols ──▶ blast radius ──▶ ┌─ scope check vs stated intent (graph diff) (graph impact) ├─ minimal sufficient test set └─ radius summary │ one PR comment, every claim linked to the graph path that proves it ``` It posts a single comment like: > ## 🧨 Blast Radius > **14 nodes** · 4 modules · 3 services · **3 scope findings** · **6 tests (2 gaps)** > > **Scope check** — intent: *"add rate limiting to the redirect endpoint"* (source: `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer) > > | | Changed symbol | Why flagged | Dependents | > |--|--|--|--| > | 🔴 | `Database.query` `src/db/database.ts:41` | not referenced in intent · 9 dependents | 9 | > | 🟠 | `LinkRepo.byId` `src/repo/link-repo.ts:12` | not referenced in intent · 4 dependents | 4 | > > **Recommended tests (6)** — covers all but 2 changed symbols > ```bash > npx vitest run test/redirect.test.ts test/rate-limit.test.ts test/link-repo.test.ts -t "redirect|rate|byId" > ``` >
Full blast radius (14 nodes) …
Every row links to an **evidence block** that names the exact graph path (`Database.query` → called by `LinkRepo.byId` → called by `RedirectService` → covered by `redirect.test.ts`), so the reviewer can verify each flag instead of trusting it. ## How it uses the graph (not just displaying it) | Graph command | What Blast Radius does with the output | | --- | --- | | `entire-graph diff --base A --head B --json` | the set of changed symbols and each one's `dependents_count` | | `entire-graph impact --symbol S --file F --json` | per-symbol callers / callees / type consumers / data flows / co-change files / siblings — unioned and deduped into the radius | | `entire-graph neighbors --symbol S --relation CALLS --direction in` | distance refinement for test ranking | | `Entire-Checkpoint:` git trailer | resolves the change back to its originating session so the *stated intent* is the real captured prompt, not a guess | The raw output is never shown on its own. It is joined, scored, and turned into a decision (approve / look here / run these) — which is the point of the track. ## Install ```bash npm install -g blast-radius # or: npx blast-radius ``` Requires **Node ≥ 20**. For live analysis it also needs the `entire-graph` binary on `PATH` (the GitHub Action builds it for you). For local development and demos you don't need it — see *Fixture mode*. ## Usage ```bash # analyse a range in the current repo, print the markdown report blast-radius review --base origin/main --head HEAD # machine-readable, for agents blast-radius review --base origin/main --head HEAD --format json # code-scanning integration blast-radius review --base origin/main --head HEAD --format sarif --out blast-radius.sarif # no entire-graph binary? run against recorded fixtures blast-radius review --fixture ./fixtures/entire-graph --format markdown ``` Key flags: `--repo `, `--intent-source pr-body,github-issue,checkpoint-trailer`, `--fail-on-findings`, `--out ` (repeatable with `--format`). ## GitHub Action ```yaml # .github/workflows/blast-radius.yml name: Blast Radius on: pull_request permissions: { contents: read, pull-requests: write, security-events: write } jobs: blast-radius: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 with: { fetch-depth: 0 } - uses: entire-hackathon/blast-radius@v0.1.0 with: base: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }} head: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }} upload-sarif: true ``` The action builds `entire-graph` (cached), runs the review, upserts one PR comment, and optionally uploads SARIF to the Code scanning tab. ## Fixture mode `FixtureGraphAdapter` reads recorded `entire-graph` JSON from a directory, so the entire pipeline — scope check, test selection, rendering — runs with **only Node installed**. Every test and the demo use this path. Recorded fixtures live in [`fixtures/entire-graph/`](fixtures/entire-graph). ## Architecture Hexagonal. Pure domain core, everything external behind a port with a test fake, single composition root, pipeline of pure stages, strategy pattern for the scope-creep heuristics. Full detail in [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Build plan and status board in [`docs/PLAN.md`](docs/PLAN.md). ``` src/domain/ pure — model, pipeline, blast-radius, scope-creep/, test-selection src/ports/ interfaces — graph-provider, intent-source, report-sink, renderer src/adapters/ entire-graph CLI, fixtures, gh, sinks, renderers src/app/ the review use-case + config src/composition-root.ts the only file that wires adapters ``` ## Development ```bash npm ci npm test # vitest, runs on fixtures, no binary needed npm run typecheck npm run lint # includes the hexagonal import-boundary rule npm run build ``` ## License MIT.

Nobody flagged it because nobody cross-checked the diff against the original intent. ## What Blast Radius does On every PR, it runs a pipeline over the Entire Graph: ``` changed symbols ──▶ blast radius ──▶ ┌─ scope check vs stated intent (graph diff) (graph impact) ├─ minimal sufficient test set └─ radius summary │ one PR comment, every claim linked to the graph path that proves it ``` It posts a single comment like: > ## 🧨 Blast Radius > **14 nodes** · 4 modules · 3 services · **3 scope findings** · **6 tests (2 gaps)** > > **Scope check** — intent: *"add rate limiting to the redirect endpoint"* (source: `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer) > > | | Changed symbol | Why flagged | Dependents | > |--|--|--|--| > | 🔴 | `Database.query` `src/db/database.ts:41` | not referenced in intent · 9 dependents | 9 | > | 🟠 | `LinkRepo.byId` `src/repo/link-repo.ts:12` | not referenced in intent · 4 dependents | 4 | > > **Recommended tests (6)** — covers all but 2 changed symbols > ```bash > npx vitest run test/redirect.test.ts test/rate-limit.test.ts test/link-repo.test.ts -t "redirect|rate|byId" > ``` >
Full blast radius (14 nodes) …
Every row links to an **evidence block** that names the exact graph path (`Database.query` → called by `LinkRepo.byId` → called by `RedirectService` → covered by `redirect.test.ts`), so the reviewer can verify each flag instead of trusting it. ## How it uses the graph (not just displaying it) | Graph command | What Blast Radius does with the output | | --- | --- | | `entire-graph diff --base A --head B --json` | the set of changed symbols and each one's `dependents_count` | | `entire-graph impact --symbol S --file F --json` | per-symbol callers / callees / type consumers / data flows / co-change files / siblings — unioned and deduped into the radius | | `entire-graph neighbors --symbol S --relation CALLS --direction in` | distance refinement for test ranking | | `Entire-Checkpoint:` git trailer | resolves the change back to its originating session so the *stated intent* is the real captured prompt, not a guess | The raw output is never shown on its own. It is joined, scored, and turned into a decision (approve / look here / run these) — which is the point of the track. ## Install ```bash npm install -g blast-radius # or: npx blast-radius ``` Requires **Node ≥ 20**. For live analysis it also needs the `entire-graph` binary on `PATH` (the GitHub Action builds it for you). For local development and demos you don't need it — see *Fixture mode*. ## Usage ```bash # analyse a range in the current repo, print the markdown report blast-radius review --base origin/main --head HEAD # machine-readable, for agents blast-radius review --base origin/main --head HEAD --format json # code-scanning integration blast-radius review --base origin/main --head HEAD --format sarif --out blast-radius.sarif # no entire-graph binary? run against recorded fixtures blast-radius review --fixture ./fixtures/entire-graph --format markdown ``` Key flags: `--repo `, `--intent-source pr-body,github-issue,checkpoint-trailer`, `--fail-on-findings`, `--out ` (repeatable with `--format`). ## GitHub Action ```yaml # .github/workflows/blast-radius.yml name: Blast Radius on: pull_request permissions: { contents: read, pull-requests: write, security-events: write } jobs: blast-radius: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 with: { fetch-depth: 0 } - uses: entire-hackathon/blast-radius@v0.1.0 with: base: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }} head: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }} upload-sarif: true ``` The action builds `entire-graph` (cached), runs the review, upserts one PR comment, and optionally uploads SARIF to the Code scanning tab. ## Fixture mode `FixtureGraphAdapter` reads recorded `entire-graph` JSON from a directory, so the entire pipeline — scope check, test selection, rendering — runs with **only Node installed**. Every test and the demo use this path. Recorded fixtures live in [`fixtures/entire-graph/`](fixtures/entire-graph). ## Architecture Hexagonal. Pure domain core, everything external behind a port with a test fake, single composition root, pipeline of pure stages, strategy pattern for the scope-creep heuristics. Full detail in [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Build plan and status board in [`docs/PLAN.md`](docs/PLAN.md). ``` src/domain/ pure — model, pipeline, blast-radius, scope-creep/, test-selection src/ports/ interfaces — graph-provider, intent-source, report-sink, renderer src/adapters/ entire-graph CLI, fixtures, gh, sinks, renderers src/app/ the review use-case + config src/composition-root.ts the only file that wires adapters ``` ## Development ```bash npm ci npm test # vitest, runs on fixtures, no binary needed npm run typecheck npm run lint # includes the hexagonal import-boundary rule npm run build ``` ## License MIT.

## The idea, sharpened

Not "show me the graph." It's a **decision pipeline**: changed symbols → blast radius → three parallel checks (scope drift vs intent · minimal test set · radius summary) → one PR comment where every claim links to the graph path that proves it. Graph is a consumed dependency (`diff` + `impact` + `neighbors` joined and scored), never displayed raw. That's exactly what Track 02 asks for.

## Key decisions I made (override any of these now)

| Decision | Why | Alternative |
|---|---|---|
| **Hexagonal / ports + adapters**, pure domain core, single composition root | Every plausible curveball becomes *one adapter or one strategy*, not a rewrite. §9 of ARCHITECTURE has the table. | — |
| **Composite GitHub Action** (shell steps, no bundled JS) | No `dist/` webpack pain in a 12h window; `gh` is already on the runner | JS action w/ Octokit |
| **Fixture mode** — pipeline runs on recorded graph JSON with only Node | You dev + demo on Windows with no Go toolchain; tests are fast and offline | build entire-graph locally |
| **Intent priority: checkpoint trailer → linked issue → PR body** | Works on *any* repo today, gets sharper with Entire. Judges' mental model of "intent" is the PR description. | checkpoint-only (needs Entire CLI you don't have) |
| **Scope-creep v1 = keyword-overlap + dependents-threshold**, no embeddings | Explainable in a live demo; embeddings are a stretch, not v1 | ML similarity |
| **Extra outputs: JSON + SARIF** | SARIF → GitHub code-scanning tab = "workflow integration" points **and** a ready hedge if the curveball is "machine-verifiable output" | markdown only |
| Demo repo = **"linkshrink"**, a ~12-file TS service; staged PR adds rate-limiting **and** changes `Database.query` signature | Clean 60-second story: small intent, wide real radius, 3 flags | fork an OSS repo |

## Status right now

- ✅ ARCHITECTURE.md, PLAN.md, README.md written + committed
- ⏳ `entire-graph` compiling in a Linux Docker container (CGO + tree-sitter, slow — capturing real fixtures when it lands; falls back to hand-crafted fixtures from the JSON schema if it fails)
- ⬜ Next: P0 scaffold (package.json, tsconfig, vitest, eslint boundaries rule), then P1 domain model — TDD from there

**Two things from you:**
1. Thumbs up on the design above (or tell me what to change).
2. Create the GitHub repos when you're ready: `gh repo create blast-radius --public --source=C:\Users\amond07\Workspace\bangalore_tech_week\blast-radius --remote=origin` and one for `blast-radius-demo`. Not blocking — I'll keep building locally.

119	/** camelCase / snake_case / kebab / dotted / slashed -> lowercase word list. */
120	export function splitIdentifier(raw: string): string[] {
121	  return raw
122	    .replace(/[/\\.]+/g, " ")
123	    .replace(/([a-z0-9])([A-Z])/g, "$1 $2")
124	    .replace(/([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])/g, "$1 $2")
125	    .replace(/[_-]+/g, " ")
126	    .toLowerCase()
127	    .split(/\s+/)
128	    .filter(Boolean);
129	}
130	
131	/** Naive suffix stemmer — enough to make "limiter"/"limiting"/"limits" collide. */
132	export function stem(word: string): string {
133	  return word
134	    .replace(/(ies)$/, "y")
135	    .replace(/(ing|edly|ed|ly|es|s)$/, "")
136	    .replace(/(er|or)$/, "");
137	}

139	function normalize(words: Iterable<string>): Set<string> {
140	  const out = new Set<string>();
141	  for (const w of words) {
142	    if (w.length < 3) continue;
143	    if (STOPWORDS.has(w)) continue;
144	    const s = stem(w);
145	    if (s.length >= 3 && !STOPWORDS.has(s)) out.add(s);
146	  }
147	  return out;
148	}

150	/** Keywords for an intent text. `backtickedTerms` are weighted in as-is. */
151	export function extractKeywords(text: string): string[] {
152	  // pull `code spans` and Capitalised identifiers before generic splitting
153	  const spans = [...text.matchAll(/`([^`]+)`/g)].flatMap((m) => splitIdentifier(m[1] ?? ""));
154	  const words = splitIdentifier(text.replace(/`[^`]+`/g, " "));
155	  return [...normalize([...spans, ...words])].sort();
156	}

158	/** Tokens that identify a symbol: its qualified name + the meaningful path parts. */
159	export function symbolTokens(qualifiedName: string, file: string | undefined): Set<string> {
160	  const fromName = splitIdentifier(qualifiedName);
161	  const fromFile = file
162	    ? splitIdentifier(file.replace(/\.[a-z0-9]+$/i, "")).filter(
163	        (p) => !["src", "internal", "pkg", "lib", "app", "cmd", "test", "tests"].includes(p),
164	      )
165	    : [];
166	  return normalize([...fromName, ...fromFile]);

170	export function extractIssueRefs(text: string): string[] {
171	  const refs = new Set<string>();
172	  for (const m of text.matchAll(/(?:^|\s)(?:closes?|fixes?|resolves?|ref)?\s*#(\d+)/gi)) {
173	    refs.add(`#${m[1]}`);
174	  }
175	  for (const m of text.matchAll(/\b([\w.-]+\/[\w.-]+)#(\d+)\b/g)) {
176	    refs.add(`${m[1]}#${m[2]}`);
177	  }

187	/** Fraction of a symbol's tokens that appear in the intent keyword set. */
188	export function keywordOverlap(
189	  qualifiedName: string,
190	  file: string | undefined,
191	  intentKeywords: readonly string[],
192	): OverlapResult {
193	  const tokens = symbolTokens(qualifiedName, file);
194	  if (tokens.size === 0) return { overlap: 1, shared: [], symbolTokenCount: 0 };

120	export function splitIdentifier(raw: string): string[] {
121	  return raw
122	    .replace(/[/\\.]+/g, " ")
123	    .replace(/([a-z0-9])([A-Z])/g, "$1 $2")
124	    .replace(/([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])/g, "$1 $2")
125	    .replace(/[_-]+/g, " ")
126	    .toLowerCase()
127	    .split(/\s+/)
128	    .filter(Boolean);
129	}

131	/** Naive suffix stemmer — enough to make "limiter"/"limiting"/"limits" collide. */
132	export function stem(word: string): string {
133	  return word
134	    .replace(/(ies)$/, "y")
135	    .replace(/(ing|edly|ed|ly|es|s)$/, "")
136	    .replace(/(er|or)$/, "");
137	}

139	function normalize(words: Iterable<string>): Set<string> {
140	  const out = new Set<string>();
141	  for (const w of words) {
142	    if (w.length < 3) continue;
143	    if (STOPWORDS.has(w)) continue;
144	    const s = stem(w);
145	    if (s.length >= 3 && !STOPWORDS.has(s)) out.add(s);
146	  }
147	  return out;
148	}

150	/** Keywords for an intent text. `backtickedTerms` are weighted in as-is. */
151	export function extractKeywords(text: string): string[] {
152	  // pull `code spans` and Capitalised identifiers before generic splitting
153	  const spans = [...text.matchAll(/`([^`]+)`/g)].flatMap((m) => splitIdentifier(m[1] ?? ""));
154	  const words = splitIdentifier(text.replace(/`[^`]+`/g, " "));
155	  return [...normalize([...spans, ...words])].sort();
156	}

158	/** Tokens that identify a symbol: its qualified name + the meaningful path parts. */
159	export function symbolTokens(qualifiedName: string, file: string | undefined): Set<string> {
160	  const fromName = splitIdentifier(qualifiedName);
161	  const fromFile = file
162	    ? splitIdentifier(file.replace(/\.[a-z0-9]+$/i, "")).filter(
163	        (p) => !["src", "internal", "pkg", "lib", "app", "cmd", "test", "tests"].includes(p),
164	      )
165	    : [];
166	  return normalize([...fromName, ...fromFile]);
167	}

169	/** Extract `#123` / `GH-123` / `owner/repo#123` issue references from text. */
170	export function extractIssueRefs(text: string): string[] {
171	  const refs = new Set<string>();
172	  for (const m of text.matchAll(/(?:^|\s)(?:closes?|fixes?|resolves?|ref)?\s*#(\d+)/gi)) {
173	    refs.add(`#${m[1]}`);
174	  }
175	  for (const m of text.matchAll(/\b([\w.-]+\/[\w.-]+)#(\d+)\b/g)) {
176	    refs.add(`${m[1]}#${m[2]}`);
177	  }
178	  return [...refs];
179	}

181	export interface OverlapResult {
182	  readonly overlap: number;
183	  readonly shared: string[];
184	  readonly symbolTokenCount: number;
185	}
186	
187	/** Fraction of a symbol's tokens that appear in the intent keyword set. */
188	export function keywordOverlap(
189	  qualifiedName: string,
190	  file: string | undefined,
191	  intentKeywords: readonly string[],
192	): OverlapResult {
193	  const tokens = symbolTokens(qualifiedName, file);
194	  if (tokens.size === 0) return { overlap: 1, shared: [], symbolTokenCount: 0 };
195	  const kw = new Set(intentKeywords);
196	  const shared = [...tokens].filter((t) => kw.has(t));
197	  return { overlap: shared.length / tokens.size, shared, symbolTokenCount: tokens.size };
198	}

input.content:
name: "Blast Radius"
description: "Impact-aware PR review powered by Entire Graph — blast radius, scope-drift check, minimal test set."
branding:
  icon: "target"
  color: "orange"

inputs:
  base:
    description: "Base revision (default: the PR base sha)."
    required: false
  head:
    description: "Head revision (default: the PR head sha)."
    required: false
  entire-graph-ref:
    description: "git ref of entireio/entire-graph to build."
    required: false
    default: "main"
  intent-source:
    description: "Comma list, in priority order."
    required: false
    default: "checkpoint-trailer,github-issue,pr-body"
  fail-on-findings:
    description: "Fail the check when scope findings exist."
    required: false
    default: "false"
  upload-sarif:
    description: "Upload findings to the Code scanning tab."
    required: false
    default: "false"
  comment:
    description: "Upsert the report as a PR comment."
    required: false
    default: "true"
  blast-radius-ref:
    description: "npm spec or github: spec for the CLI (default: this action's repo@version)."
    required: false
    default: "github:entire-hackathon/blast-radius"

runs:
  using: "composite"
  steps:
    - name: Set up Go
      uses: actions/setup-go@v5
      with:
        go-version: "1.26"
        cache: false

    - name: Restore entire-graph binary
      id: cache-eg
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.local/bin/entire-graph
        key: entire-graph-${{ runner.os }}-${{ inputs.entire-graph-ref }}

    - name: Build entire-graph
      if: steps.cache-eg.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
        git clone --depth 1 --branch "${{ inputs.entire-graph-ref }}" \
          https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph "$tmp"
        ( cd "$tmp" && CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -trimpath -o entire-graph ./cmd/entire-graph )
        mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
        mv "$tmp/entire-graph" ~/.local/bin/entire-graph

    - name: Add entire-graph to PATH
      shell: bash
      run: echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

    - name: Run Blast Radius
      shell: bash
      env:
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        args=(review --repo . --graph-head)
        [ -n "${{ inputs.base }}" ] && args+=(--base "${{ inputs.base }}")
        [ -n "${{ inputs.head }}" ] && args+=(--head "${{ inputs.head }}")
        args+=(--intent-source "${{ inputs.intent-source }}")
        args+=(--format markdown)

name: "Blast Radius"
description: "Impact-aware PR review powered by Entire Graph — blast radius, scope-drift check, minimal test set."
branding:
  icon: "target"
  color: "orange"

inputs:
  base:
    description: "Base revision (default: the PR base sha)."
    required: false
  head:
    description: "Head revision (default: the PR head sha)."
    required: false

    required: false

    description: "Upload findings to the Code scanning tab."
    required: false
    default: "false"
  comment:
    description: "Upsert the report as a PR comment."
    required: false
    default: "true"

    description: "npm spec or github: spec for the CLI (default: this action's repo@version)."
    required: false

runs:

  steps:

      uses: actions/setup-go@v5
      with:

    - name: Restore entire-graph binary

      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.local/bin/entire-graph
        key: entire-graph-${{ runner.os }}-${{ inputs.entire-graph-ref }}

# linkshrink

A tiny URL shortener — the demo service for
[**Blast Radius**](https://github.com/entire-hackathon/blast-radius).

```
http/router.ts
  ├─ GET /:slug   → http/redirect-handler.ts → service/redirect.ts ─┐
  └─ POST /shorten → service/shorten.ts ───────────────────────────┤
                                                                    ▼
                                          repo/link-repo.ts  (byId / save / hit)
                                                                    ▼
                                              db/database.ts  (Database.query)
```

Everything funnels through `Database.query`, which is what makes it a good demo:
a change there has a blast radius the diff never shows.

## The demo PR

Branch `feat/redirect-rate-limit` is a staged pull request. Its stated intent
(captured as an Entire checkpoint) is:

> add token-bucket rate limiting to the redirect endpoint so abusive clients get 429s

The diff does that — **and also** changes `Database.query`'s signature, rippling
through every method in `LinkRepo`. Blast Radius flags the second part as scope
drift and recommends the tests that actually cover the change.

## Run the tests

```bash
npm install
npm test
```

# Demo script (90 seconds)

## Setup (before you present)

- `blast-radius-demo` repo pushed to GitHub, Action installed.
- PR open: `feat/redirect-rate-limit` → `main`.
- A terminal in `blast-radius/` for the offline fallback.
- Screen recording of the whole arc already saved (network insurance).

## The arc

1. **Frame it (10s).** Open the PR. Read the title: *"Rate-limit the redirect
   endpoint."* "Small, contained change — I'd normally skim this and approve."

2. **The comment (20s).** Scroll to the Blast Radius comment.
   > **17 nodes · 6 modules · 4 scope findings · 2 tests**
   "It touched 17 graph nodes. Four of them are outside what the ticket asked
   for."

3. **The scope table (20s).** Point at `Database.query` — 🟠, 6 dependents,
   *"no vocabulary overlap with the stated intent."* Then the three `LinkRepo`
   methods under it. "The PR also re-plumbed the entire data-access layer to
   thread a new options argument. Nothing in the ticket says that."

4. **Verify a flag (20s).** Expand *Evidence*. Read the graph path:
   `Database.query → LinkRepo.byId → ShortenService.create`. Click the
   `src/db/database.ts:12` link — lands on the signature change. "Every flag is
   backed by a path through the graph I can check."

5. **The tests (15s).** "And instead of running the whole suite —"
   ```bash
   npx vitest run test/redirect.test.ts test/link-repo.test.ts
   ```
   Run it. Green. "Two files, ranked by graph distance, cover every changed
   function."

6. **Land it (5s).** "Blast Radius uses Entire Graph as a dependency — `diff`,
   `impact`, and the checkpoint trailer, joined into one decision. Raw graph
   output alone wasn't the point; the workflow is."

## Offline fallback (if the Action / network misbehaves)

```bash
cd blast-radius
npx blast-radius review \
  --fixture fixtures/scenarios/redirect-rate-limit \
  --repo ../blast-radius-demo --head HEAD \
  --repo-slug entire-hackathon/linkshrink --suite-test-count 13
```

Same report, from recorded graph JSON, no binary needed. Show the terminal
output; the story is identical.

## If the Noon Curve Ball forces a change

1. Read the constraint, find its row in `ARCHITECTURE.md §9`.
2. Implement it as the adapter / strategy / stage that row names. Add a test.
3. `npm test`, re-run the demo command, update `test/adapters/render.test.ts`
   snapshot if the output shape changed.
4. Re-record the 20 seconds that changed. Resubmit. Check in.

name: "Blast Radius"
description: "Impact-aware PR review powered by Entire Graph — blast radius, scope-drift check, minimal test set."
branding:
  icon: "target"
  color: "orange"

inputs:
  base:
    description: "Base revision (default: the PR base sha)."
    required: false
  head:
    description: "Head revision (default: the PR head sha)."
    required: false
  entire-graph-ref:
    description: "git ref of entireio/entire-graph to build."
    required: false
    default: "main"
  intent-source:
    description: "Comma list, in priority order."
    required: false
    default: "checkpoint-trailer,github-issue,pr-body"
  fail-on-findings:
    description: "Fail the check when scope findings exist."
    required: false
    default: "false"
  upload-sarif:
    description: "Upload findings to the Code scanning tab."
    required: false
    default: "false"
  comment:
    description: "Upsert the report as a PR comment."
    required: false
    default: "true"
  blast-radius-ref:
    description: "npm spec or github: spec for the CLI (default: this action's repo@version)."
    required: false
    default: "github:entire-hackathon/blast-radius"

runs:
  using: "composite"
  steps:
    - name: Set up Go
      uses: actions/setup-go@v5
      with:
        go-version: "1.26"
        cache: false

    - name: Restore entire-graph binary
      id: cache-eg
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.local/bin/entire-graph
        key: entire-graph-${{ runner.os }}-${{ inputs.entire-graph-ref }}

    - name: Build entire-graph
      if: steps.cache-eg.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
        git clone --depth 1 --branch "${{ inputs.entire-graph-ref }}" \
          https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph "$tmp"
        ( cd "$tmp" && CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -trimpath -o entire-graph ./cmd/entire-graph )
        mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
        mv "$tmp/entire-graph" ~/.local/bin/entire-graph

    - name: Add entire-graph to PATH
      shell: bash
      run: echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

    - name: Run Blast Radius
      shell: bash
      env:
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        args=(review --repo . --graph-head)
        [ -n "${{ inputs.base }}" ] && args+=(--base "${{ inputs.base }}")
        [ -n "${{ inputs.head }}" ] && args+=(--head "${{ inputs.head }}")
        args+=(--intent-source "${{ inputs.intent-source }}")
        args+=(--format markdown)
        [ "${{ inputs.comment }}" = "true" ] && args+=(--comment)
        [ "${{ inputs.upload-sarif }}" = "true" ] && args+=(--format sarif --sarif-out "$RUNNER_TEMP/blast-radius.sarif")
        [ "${{ inputs.fail-on-findings }}" = "true" ] && args+=(--fail-on-findings)
        npx --yes "${{ inputs.blast-radius-ref }}" "${args[@]}"

    - name: Upload SARIF
      if: inputs.upload-sarif == 'true'
      uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
      with:
        sarif_file: ${{ runner.temp }}/blast-radius.sarif
        category: blast-radius

name: "Blast Radius"
description: "Impact-aware PR review powered by Entire Graph — blast radius, scope-drift check, minimal test set."
branding:
  icon: "target"
  color: "orange"

inputs:
  base:
    description: "Base revision (default: the PR base sha)."
    required: false
  head:
    description: "Head revision (default: the PR head sha)."
    required: false
  entire-graph-ref:
    description: "git ref of entireio/entire-graph to build."
    required: false
    default: "main"
  intent-source:
    description: "Comma list, in priority order."
    required: false
    default: "checkpoint-trailer,github-issue,pr-body"
  fail-on-findings:
    description: "Fail the check when scope findings exist."
    required: false
    default: "false"
  upload-sarif:
    description: "Upload findings to the Code scanning tab."
    required: false
    default: "false"
  comment:
    description: "Upsert the report as a PR comment."
    required: false
    default: "true"
  dependents-threshold:
    description: "Wide-reaching-change threshold."
    required: false
    default: ""

runs:
  using: "composite"
  steps:
    - name: Set up Go
      uses: actions/setup-go@v5
      with:
        go-version: "1.26"
        cache: false

    - name: Set up Node
      uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: "22"

    - name: Restore entire-graph binary
      id: cache-eg
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.local/bin/entire-graph
        key: entire-graph-${{ runner.os }}-${{ inputs.entire-graph-ref }}

    - name: Build entire-graph
      if: steps.cache-eg.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
        git clone --depth 1 --branch "${{ inputs.entire-graph-ref }}" \
          https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph "$tmp"
        ( cd "$tmp" && CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -trimpath -o entire-graph ./cmd/entire-graph )
        mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
        mv "$tmp/entire-graph" ~/.local/bin/entire-graph

    - name: Build the CLI
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        cd "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH"
        npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
        npm run build

    - name: Run Blast Radius
      shell: bash
      env:
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
        args=(review --repo "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" --graph-head)
        [ -n "${{ inputs.base }}" ] && args+=(--base "${{ inputs.base }}")
        [ -n "${{ inputs.head }}" ] && args+=(--head "${{ inputs.head }}")
        args+=(--intent-source "${{ inputs.intent-source }}")
        [ -n "${{ inputs.dependents-threshold }}" ] && args+=(--dependents-threshold "${{ inputs.dependents-threshold }}")
        args+=(--format markdown)
        [ "${{ inputs.comment }}" = "true" ] && args+=(--comment)
        [ "${{ inputs.upload-sarif }}" = "true" ] && args+=(--format sarif --sarif-out "$RUNNER_TEMP/blast-radius.sarif")
        [ "${{ inputs.fail-on-findings }}" = "true" ] && args+=(--fail-on-findings)
        node "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/dist/cli.js" "${args[@]}"

    - name: Upload SARIF
      if: inputs.upload-sarif == 'true' && hashFiles(format('{0}/blast-radius.sarif', runner.temp)) != ''
      uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
      with:
        sarif_file: ${{ runner.temp }}/blast-radius.sarif
        category: blast-radius

115	    if (isErr(res)) {
116	      log("error", `publish to ${sink.kind} failed: ${res.error.message}`);
117	      sinkErrors.push({ sink: sink.kind, message: res.error.message });

120	    publishedTo.push(`${renderer.format}→${sink.kind}`);

124	    return err(BlastRadiusError.sink(sinkErrors.map((e) => `${e.sink}: ${e.message}`).join("; ")));
125	  }

description: Build/runner/CI specifics for the Blast Radius hackathon project
metadata:
  type: project

Working notes for [[blast-radius-hackathon]].

- **No Go toolchain on the user's Windows box.** `entire-graph` is built for Linux in
  Docker: `docker run --rm -v ...:/src golang:1.26-bookworm bash -c "apt-get install -y gcc g++ && CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -o entire-graph-linux ./cmd/entire-graph"`. Runs ~4 min cold.
- **`entire-graph impact --profile full` rebuilds the whole index per call** (~220s on the
  entire-graph repo; fast on the tiny demo repo). The Action warms `actions/cache` on the
  binary and passes `--graph-head`.
- **`gh` in Claude's Bash is NOT authed** by default — `git push` works (credential manager)
  but `gh` needs the user to have run `gh auth login`. Once authed, `gh pr create` / `gh run`
  work from Claude.
- **Force-push via Claude Bash:** `git push --force` was blocked by the auto-mode classifier;
  `git push --force` of a *tag* went through. Branch force-pushes: hand the user the command.
- **Org pins `GITHUB_TOKEN` workflow permissions** (repo setting greyed out) — but a workflow
  declaring `permissions: pull-requests: write` still posted the PR comment fine. The Action
  also always writes the report to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` as a no-permission fallback, and a
  failing sink is non-fatal (`runReview` collects `sinkErrors`, only fatal if every sink fails).
- **CI gotcha:** `prettier --check .` chokes on the captured single-line fixture JSON —
  `.prettierignore` excludes `fixtures/`, `test/fixtures/`, `__snapshots__/`.
- **Action invokes the CLI in-place** (`cd $GITHUB_ACTION_PATH && npm ci && npm run build`,
  then `node $GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/dist/cli.js`), not `npx github:` — `dist/` is gitignored.
- Demo `Entire-Checkpoint: cp_demo01` trailer is on the PR head commit; captured intent is
  `blast-radius-demo/.entire/intent/cp_demo01.json` (`{prompt|title|body}`).

- captures the session (including the prompt the developer gave the agent) as a "checkpoint"

Concrete walkthrough. You have a normal GitHub repo, JS/TS/Python/Go, with some tests. You want Blast Radius on your PRs.

## What the user does — one file, once

Create `.github/workflows/blast-radius.yml` in their repo:

```yaml
name: Blast Radius
on: pull_request

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  security-events: write

jobs:
  blast-radius:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: entire-hackathon/blast-radius@v0.1.0
        with:
          upload-sarif: true
```

Commit it. **That's the entire setup.** No intent file, no Entire account, no config.

## What happens automatically from then on

Every time someone opens a PR:

1. The Action builds `entire-graph` (cached after the first run) and runs it on the PR's diff.
2. It figures out the **intent** by itself:
   - Reads the **PR description** the author typed
   - Reads any **linked issue** (`Closes #12`)
   - *(If the repo happens to use Entire, it also reads the checkpoint prompt — but that's a bonus, not required)*
3. It computes the blast radius, checks it against that intent, picks the tests.
4. It posts **one comment** on the PR. Done.

So for a fresh repo, the answer to "what does the user do?":

| | |
|--|--|
| **Add** | one 15-line workflow file |
| **Write** | a normal PR description (which they'd write anyway) |
| **Install / configure** | nothing |
| **Create an intent file** | **no** |

## The demo repo is a special case

`blast-radius-demo` has that `.entire/intent/cp_demo01.json` file **only to demonstrate tier 2** (the "Entire is in the loop" path) without needing a real Entire server. A normal user never touches it — their intent comes from the PR description they already write.

## If they don't want the Action — local CLI

```bash
npx blast-radius review --base main --head HEAD
```
Prints the same report in the terminal. Needs `entire-graph` on PATH for that. Same intent logic (reads the current branch's PR/commit info).

content.text:
Here's the full technical picture, in layers. Learn these five and you can field anything.

---

## Layer 1 — What `entire-graph` builds (you depend on this, don't reimplement it)

`entire-graph` parses every file with **tree-sitter** (real grammars, not regex) and emits a **typed graph**:

- **Nodes** = symbols: functions, methods, classes, types, fields — each with a stable id, `qualified_name`, `file:line`, language, kind.
- **Edges** = ~30 relation types. The ones you use:
  | edge | meaning |
  |---|---|
  | `CALLS` | A calls B (resolved from the call site, tree-sitter-accurate) |
  | `USES_TYPE` / `PARAM_TYPE` / `RETURNS_TYPE` | A references type B in its body / params / return |
  | `DATA_FLOWS` | a value flows from A to B (param forwarding, return threading) |
  | `FILE_CHANGES_WITH` | A's file and B's file historically change in the same commits (mined from git log) |
  | `CONTAINS` | class A contains method B (→ "siblings") |

It's **deterministic and local** — same repo + same commit = same graph, no model, no network. That matters for a judge: "our impact analysis isn't an LLM guessing, it's a parsed call graph."

---

## Layer 2 — What you ask it, per changed symbol

Two commands:

**`entire-graph diff --base <A> --head <B> --json`** → the list of changed symbols. Each row:
```json
{ "name": "Database.query", "kind": "method", "type": "signature_changed",
  "after_start_line": 12, "dependents_count": 6 }
```
`dependents_count` is entire-graph's own heuristic count of things that transitively depend on this symbol.

**`entire-graph impact --symbol "Database.query" --file src/db/database.ts --depth 2 --format json`** → a **bounded traversal outward from that one symbol**, already sectioned:
```
callers        (who calls it — incoming CALLS, depth ≤ 2)
callees        (what it calls — outgoing CALLS)
type_consumers (USES_TYPE / PARAM_TYPE / RETURNS_TYPE)
data_flows     (DATA_FLOWS edges)
co_changes     (FILE_CHANGES_WITH — git co-change)
siblings       (same CONTAINS parent)
```

Real output for `Database.query` in the demo:
```
callers (5):  LinkRepo.byId (depth 1), LinkRepo.save (1), LinkRepo.hit (1),
              RedirectService.resolve (2, via LinkRepo.byId),
              ShortenService.create (2, via LinkRepo.save)
type_consumers (4): Row (RETURNS_TYPE), QueryOptions (PARAM_TYPE), ...
co_changes (3):  <3 files that change alongside src/db/database.ts>
siblings (1):    Database.seed
```

So **`entire-graph` does the graph walk**. You don't traverse edges yourself — you call `impact` once per changed symbol.

---

## Layer 3 — Your code: turning one impact result into radius nodes

`src/domain/graph-mapping.ts` → `toRadiusNodes(rawImpact, "Database.query")`:

For every entry in every section, it produces a `RadiusNode`:
```ts
{
  ref: { qualifiedName: "LinkRepo.byId", file: "src/repo/link-repo.ts", line: 8, ... },
  section: "callers",
  relation: "CALLED_BY",           // section → relation mapping
  direction: "in",
  distance: 1,                      // = entire-graph's depth (1 = direct)
  viaChain: ["LinkRepo.byId"],      // intermediate hops, from the `via` field
  callSite: { file: "...", line: 14 },
  originSymbols: ["Database.query"], // ← tagged with WHICH changed symbol this came from
  isTest: false                     // matched against test-file globs
}
```

Key move: **every node is stamped with its origin** (`originSymbols`). That's what lets you later say "this test covers `Database.query` and `LinkRepo.byId`."

---

## Layer 4 — The fold: `computeBlastRadius()` (`src/domain/blast-radius.ts`)

You call `impact` for *each* changed symbol, so you get N node-lists that **overlap**. This function merges them into one deduplicated set. The exact algorithm:

```
byKey = {}                          // Map<"file::qualifiedName", RadiusNode>
originKeys  = {every changed symbol's key}
originNames = {every changed symbol's qualified name}
addedNames  = {changed symbols whose type == "added"}

for each node in every list:
    1. DROP if node is an external callee        (fmt.Errorf etc. — noise)
    2. DROP if node is a sibling of an added-only symbol   (members of a new class)
    3. DROP if node IS one of the changed symbols          (it's the origin, not the blast)
    4. key = "<file>::<qualifiedName>"
       if key already seen → mergeNode(existing, incoming):
           - keep the SHORTER distance
           - UNION the originSymbols
           - keep whichever has a real viaChain / callSite
           - isTest = either was a test
       else → store it

nodes = values(byKey) sorted by (distance asc, then name)
sectionTotals[section] = count of nodes in that section
```

So the **19 nodes** in your report = distinct `(file, symbol)` pairs across all 4 impact calls (Database.query, LinkRepo.byId, .save, .hit — wait, 4 changed callables + the added ones), after dropping origins/externals/added-siblings and merging duplicates.

Why dedup by `(file, qualifiedName)` and not just name: two different `query` methods in different files are different nodes; the same `LinkRepo.byId` reached from both `Database.query` and (transitively) another change is **one** node with `originSymbols: ["Database.query", ...]` and the shortest distance kept.

---

## Layer 5 — What the numbers in the report mean

| Report says | Computed from |
|---|---|
| **19 nodes** | `radius.nodes.length` |
| **8 modules** | distinct first-2 path segments across those nodes (`summary.ts`) |
| **CALLED_BY: 8 · RETURNS_TYPE: 3 · …** | `groupBy(node.relation)` |
| **`Database.query` … 6 dependents** | `dependents_count` straight from `entire-graph diff` |
| **evidence path `Database.query → ShortenService.create`** | `[originSymbol, ...node.viaChain, node.name]` for the nearest caller nodes |
| **`link-repo.test.ts` covers Database.query, LinkRepo.byId, …** | that test node's `originSymbols` (accumulated during the merge) |

---

## Be honest about the limits (judges respect this)

1. **Call resolution is static.** Dynamic dispatch, reflection, DI containers, string-keyed handlers → edges can be missed or over-approximated. entire-graph is tree-sitter-accurate for direct calls; it degrades gracefully and reports `completeness: degraded` in its JSON.
2. **`depth 2` cap.** You see direct + one hop of transitive callers, not the whole tree. Deliberate — deeper is noise for a review.
3. **`co_changes` are heuristic** (git history correlation), not causal.
4. **`dependents_count`** is entire-graph's number, not independently verified by you — you surface it, you don't recompute it.
5. **"covers every changed symbol"** means *a test exists that transitively reaches it in the graph* — not that the test asserts on the new behavior. It's test *selection*, not coverage measurement.

If a judge pushes on accuracy: *"It's a static call graph, so it's precise for direct calls and conservative elsewhere — the same tradeoff every IDE 'find usages' makes. We surface the graph path for every claim so the reviewer verifies, rather than trusting."*

content.text:
Yes — plenty. Here's the map, ordered by effort-vs-payoff. The first group is doable before submission today.

## Quick wins (each < 1 hr, real demo impact)

| Improvement | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| **Dedupe the evidence lines** | Right now when two strategies fire on one symbol you see near-duplicate "reaches X" / "dependents include X". Merge them. Pure polish, but the evidence block is what a judge reads closely. |
| **Show the call sites to fix** | `entire-graph` already gives `call_site: {file, line}` for every caller. For a `signature_changed` symbol, emit a checklist: *"9 call sites to update: `link-repo.ts:14`, `link-repo.ts:24`, …"*. Turns the tool from "warning" into "actionable." |
| **Name the `co_changes` files** | Those `FILE_CHANGES_WITH` entries currently have blank names (they're file edges, not symbols). Render them as `↔ src/http/router.ts` instead of dropping the label. |
| **"Review in this order" list** | Add one ordered checklist at the top: highest-severity finding → widest change → coverage gaps. Reviewers want a path, not a table. |
| **Breaking-change flag** | Compare old vs new signature: param added without default, return type narrowed, param removed → tag the finding `breaking`. `diff` already gives `old_signature`/`new_signature`. |

## Real improvements (0.5–2 days each — future-work slide)

1. **Smarter scope-creep than lexical overlap.**
   - **Graph-anchored:** if a changed symbol is 1–2 hops in the call graph from a symbol that *does* match the intent, it's probably legit collateral — downgrade it. ("You changed `Database.query`, but it's called directly by `RedirectService` which IS in scope" → softer flag.)
   - **Local embeddings** for semantic similarity so "throttle" matches "rate limit", "auth" matches "login". Small model, still no network at runtime.
   - **History-learned pairs:** symbols that always change together in this repo's git log aren't scope creep.

2. **Adaptive depth.** Fixed `--depth 2` misses deep ripples on a signature change. If `dependents_count > 15`, walk to depth 3–4 for that symbol only.

3. **Real coverage, not just selection.** Today "covers X" = *a test reaches X in the graph*. Cross-reference an `lcov`/coverage report if the repo produces one, and flag `signature_changed` symbols where **no test asserts the new shape**.

4. **Service-boundary awareness.** Map paths → services (from `package.json` workspaces / `go.mod` / a config file) and say *"this change crosses from `redirect-svc` into `shorten-svc`"* — the scariest kind of blast radius.

5. **Trend baseline.** "This repo's PRs touch ~7 nodes on average; this one touches 19" — anomaly signal, not just absolute numbers.

6. **Suppression.** `.blastradiusignore` or a `scope-ok` PR label so an intentional wide refactor doesn't nag on every push.

## Ambitious (the "where this goes" slide)

- **MCP / agent tool.** Wrap `review()` as an MCP server so a coding agent calls `blast_radius(base, head)` *before* it edits — "here's what you're about to affect, and the 6 tests to run after." This is the brief's "workflow for agents" taken literally. The core use-case is already pure and adapter-free, so it's a new entry point beside `cli.ts`, nothing else changes.
- **Checkpoint-native intent.** Replace the `.entire/intent/<id>.json` file read with a real `entire checkpoint show` / `entire search` call — the actual captured session, and the full "did the agent do what it was asked" loop.
- **Pre-merge gate with policy.** `fail-on-findings` exists; add policy tiers ("block if a `breaking` change has an untested caller").

## What to say to a judge who asks "what's next"

> *"Three directions. Make the scope heuristic graph-aware — a change close to an in-scope symbol is probably fine. Turn warnings into actions — list the exact call sites to fix. And expose it as an MCP tool so agents run it before editing, not just humans after."*

**"Instead of running all 13 test files, run these 4 — they're the ones that actually touch your change."** Copy the command, paste it, done.

**"Why these tests"** table — one row per selected test:

| column | meaning |
|---|---|
| **Test** | the test file, clickable to the source |
| **Covers** | which changed symbols this test reaches through the call graph. `link-repo.test.ts` reaches 7 things because it calls `LinkRepo` methods which call `Database.query` — so running it exercises the whole chain you touched |
| **Distance** | graph hops from the test to the nearest changed symbol. `1` = the test calls the changed code directly (strongest signal). A `3` would be "reaches it eventually" |

"covers every changed symbol" = every function/method you modified has at least one test in this list. If it said "covers all but 2", those 2 would be listed as **gaps** — change them and verify by hand.

### Full blast radius — 19 nodes across 11 files

> CALLED_BY: 8 · FILE_CHANGES_WITH: 4 · RETURNS_TYPE: 3 · CALLS: 2 · SIBLING: 1 · PARAM_TYPE: 1

The 19 affected nodes, **bucketed by relationship**:
- **CALLED_BY: 8** — 8 symbols call your changed code (the ripple upward)
- **FILE_CHANGES_WITH: 4** — 4 files that historically change alongside yours (git-history signal)
- **RETURNS_TYPE: 3 / PARAM_TYPE: 1** — 4 places use a type your change touches
- **CALLS: 2** — 2 things your changed code now calls
- **SIBLING: 1** — 1 method in the same class

`8 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 19`. It's a one-line profile of *how* the change spreads, not just *how much*.

## "Full node list is in the JSON / SARIF output (--format json)"

The markdown comment shows the **summary** (counts + the important findings) to keep the PR comment short. The **complete list of all 19 nodes** — every name, file, line, distance, relation — is in the machine formats:

```bash
blast-radius review --base main --head HEAD --format json    # the whole AnalysisReport object
blast-radius review --base main --head HEAD --format sarif    # findings as SARIF → GitHub "Code scanning" tab
```

The Action already produces both (SARIF goes to the Security tab, JSON is for agents/scripts). The markdown just doesn't dump all 19 rows inline because it'd bury the 4 findings that matter.

**Honestly** — I could put the full 19-row list in a collapsed `<details>` in the comment too. Right now it's a deliberate omission, not a limitation.

## Making it more visually appealing

GitHub PR comments allow more than we're using. Options, biggest impact first:

1. **A Mermaid graph diagram** — GitHub renders ```mermaid blocks inline. Show the changed symbol at the center with arrows out to its blast radius, findings in red. This literally *shows the graph* — huge for a "Graph Intelligence" track demo. ~1 hr.
2. **A scoreboard header with shield badges** — `![](https://img.shields.io/badge/nodes-19-blue)` style row instead of the plain text line. Crisper, scannable. ~20 min.
3. **Severity as colored bars / a mini bar chart** in unicode block chars for the relation breakdown. ~20 min.
4. **Full 19-node list** in a collapsed section with a clean table. ~15 min.
5. **Job summary** can take even richer HTML than the comment — could make that version fancier.

I'd do **#1 (mermaid) + #2 (badges) + #4 (full list)**. Want me to build that into the renderer now? It's a contained change to `src/adapters/render/markdown.ts` plus a new mermaid helper — tests stay green, and the demo comment gets dramatically better.
